metalcraft.options.title: MetalCraft Settings
metalcraft.options.half_resolution.descr: Render at macOS logical resolution instead of the Retina display's 2x backing resolution. The image is upscaled to the native Metal surface for a substantial GPU performance gain.
metalcraft.options.half_resolution.toolt: Halves each framebuffer dimension, reducing the rendered pixel count to one quarter.
metalcraft.options.unlocked_frame_rate.t: Presents without display synchronization and ignores Minecraft's Max Framerate and one-minute AFK limits, so frames are not paced to the display's refresh rate. Iconified, ten-minute idle, and menu throttles still apply.
metalcraft.water.water_enabled.tooltip: Animated water, reflections, absorption, foam, and underwater distortion. Off restores the original water appearance.
metalcraft.water.water_wave_strength.too: Surface ripple strength. Zero keeps the water surface normal still.
metalcraft.water.water_refraction_streng: Background distortion through water. Zero removes distortion while preserving depth absorption.
metalcraft.water.water_absorption.toolti: How strongly depth colors and dims the view through water. Zero keeps background transmission clear.
metalcraft.water.water_foam.tooltip: Restrained foam at shallow contacts. Zero disables foam.
metalcraft.water.water_underwater_distor: Mild distortion of the world while submerged. Zero disables distortion; underwater fog remains.
metalcraft.water.water_reflection_qualit: Baseline reflects the sky and sun. Screen-space tiers also reflect visible opaque objects, at extra cost. Off-screen and transparent objects use the baseline fallback.
metalcraft.water.water_detail_distance.t: Range of detailed water waves. Larger waves preserve distant reflections. Limited to loaded terrain; tiny ripples remain filtered to reduce shimmer.
metalcraft.water.water_detail.tooltip: Fine surface ripples. None retains broad waves; higher levels add smaller ripples. Larger waves retain distant surface detail.
metalcraft.lod.title: Level of Detail…
metalcraft.lod.pending_geometry: Terrain LOD is under development. Tuning is saved, but rendering remains at full detail.
metalcraft.lod.requires_metal: Terrain LOD requires the Metal graphics backend.
metalcraft.lod.preset.tooltip: Changes full-detail radius and geometry error together. Manual tuning selects Custom.
metalcraft.lod.radius.tooltip: Keeps nearby terrain at full detail. Near-plane and screen-error safeguards also apply.
metalcraft.lod.error.tooltip: Maximum projected geometry error in scene pixels. Lower values retain more detail.
metalcraft.lod.pending_stages: Reduced-resolution shading and diagnostics remain unavailable. Minecraft render and simulation distances are unchanged.
metalcraft.lod.horizon.tooltip: Opaque distant terrain fills progressively. Single-player can generate unseen chunks; multiplayer remembers received terrain. Distant fluids remain absent. Dense terrain may exceed the cache budget; 256 chunks is a stress setting. Disk cache must be on.
metalcraft.lod.generation.tooltip: Single-player only: generate and save terrain outward toward the LOD horizon without extending simulation. Uses background CPU and world disk space. Turn off to retain explored-terrain caching only. Background work controls the pace.
metalcraft.lod.generation.remote: This server supplies terrain within its own view distance. Received terrain is cached normally; no server mod is required.
metalcraft.lod.experimental_geometry: Distant terrain preview. Larger horizons add generation and rendering work and may reduce FPS. Keep LOD off for ordinary 16-chunk play.
metalcraft.lod.unsupported_pack: Terrain LOD currently supports the Standard pack and no shader pack.
metalcraft.lod.smoothing.tooltip: Limits coarsening to one tier per frame. Nearby detail and shared boundaries remain protected.
metalcraft.lod.memory.tooltip: Limits LOD GPU allocations, including resources still in flight. Keeps headroom for the rest of the renderer.
metalcraft.lod.work.tooltip: Bounds concurrent LOD builds and upload bytes per frame. Higher settings prepare detail sooner but add work.
metalcraft.options.native_distance: Render Distance supports up to 256 chunks through Minecraft's normal chunk pipeline. Terrain LOD reduces distant opaque surface detail. Multiplayer remains limited by the server, and higher distances still use more memory.
metalcraft.options.native_lod_pixels.too: Shade distant solid terrain at half/quarter resolution, keeping near terrain and depth sharp. Requires Terrain LOD and the None shader pack. Other packs retain their normal resolution. Disable to compare performance.
metalcraft.options.native_quality_distan: Full terrain detail within this horizontal distance (1–256 chunks; default 4). Beyond it, terrain uses shell models. Zoom refines the shell without restoring individual blocks. Measured to the nearest chunk boundary. Requires terrain LOD and reduction above 0.
0 keeps native detail everywhere. Higher levels simplify distant shell models more quickly, up to one coarse exterior shape per section. Nearby terrain stays sharp. 3 is the default. Requires terrain LOD enabled; changes apply as chunks rebuild.
metalcraft.options.native_lod.tooltip: Render distant terrain as simple exterior shell models. Nearby terrain keeps its normal blocks. Shells omit small details, cavities and distant block entities; fluids keep their normal rendering. Changes apply as chunks rebuild.
metalcraft.options.clear_distance_fog.to: Keeps distant terrain clear in fair weather by pushing distance fog beyond the loaded view. Water, lava, snow, weather and status-effect fog remain. Applies immediately on Metal.
